{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-sd-x","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"18d086e8f63fe594132c8e833140388eb902acefabc2300f54698fdf42f6c91c","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-sd-class-std:lineage:73","source_registry_sha256":"a4e51960bfe4da242ea11046073ac8d3d0353ce120a5409a11c1f9ab4c4da57a","source_liveness_sha256":"1aea607665fc1312b9a6988c94545b32e414886d6d428b2b6d66e4261f9397f1"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C2"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C2","chunk_id":"C2.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Sharing the road","heading":"C2 — Knowledge continuation and confusables: Sharing the road","learner_facing":false,"markdown":"## C2 — Knowledge continuation and confusables: Sharing the road

FACT_ID: sec17-R01 | anchor: A63
A large truck or bus has blind areas beside, behind and in front of it. [A63]
Source: [A63 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec17-R02 | anchor: A63
A truck’s right blind area begins behind the cab and may extend along the truck’s full length. [A63]
Source: [A63 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec17-R03 | anchor: A63
If the commercial driver’s face is not visible in the side mirror, avoid assuming the driver can see you. [A63]
Source: [A63 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec17-R04 | anchor: A63
Stay beside a large vehicle only as long as needed because a lane change or swerve can create a crash. [A63]
Source: [A63 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec17-R05 | anchor: A63
This page’s loaded-truck example gives at least 335 feet to stop from 55 miles per hour under ideal conditions with good tires and adjusted brakes. [A63]
Source: [A63 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec17-R06 | anchor: A63
The same page describes the truck stopping example as more than one-and-a-half times a car’s stopping distance. [A63]
Source: [A63 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec17-R07 | anchor: A63
Do not cut into a large vehicle’s stopping space, and after passing wait until its whole front appears in the mirror before moving ahead and maintaining speed. [A63]
Source: [A63 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec17-R08 | anchor: A63
A large vehicle’s rear blind area can extend up to 200 feet, so do not follow close enough to lose its driver’s view or your view ahead. [A63]
Source: [A63 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec17-R09 | anchor: A63
Position a following vehicle where the truck driver can see it in the side mirrors. [A63]
Source: [A63 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec17-R10 | anchor: A63
The handbook describes large vehicles using the right lane around 35 miles per hour on steep hills and advises avoiding that lane where possible on hills and near weigh-station reentry. [A63]
Source: [A63 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec17-R11 | anchor: A63
Give a turning truck or bus room because it may swing left or use another lane before completing a right turn. [A63]
Source: [A63 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec17-R12 | anchor: A63
Do not move between a right-turning large vehicle and the curb; wait until its turn is complete. [A63]
Source: [A63 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec17-R13 | anchor: A63
When meeting an opposing truck, keep as far right as possible to reduce sideswipe and wind-turbulence effects. [A63]
Source: [A63 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec17-R14 | anchor: A63
If unsure about an oncoming truck or bus’s speed, do not turn left in front of it. [A63]
Source: [A63 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec17-R15 | anchor: A63
Stop behind marked stop lines to preserve the turning room they provide for large vehicles. [A63]
Source: [A63 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec17-R16 | anchor: A63
Do not cut off a large vehicle to reach an exit, turn or narrow construction lane. [A63]
Source: [A63 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec17-R17 | anchor: A63
Merge with traffic speed and do not move in front of a truck or bus and then slow. [A63]
Source: [A63 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec17-R18 | anchor: A63
A truck or bus stopped on an acceleration lane needs substantial distance to regain merging speed; steady traffic pace can help it enter without another stop. [A63]
Source: [A63 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec17-R19 | anchor: A64
Never park on a runaway truck ramp or its entrance because a vehicle unable to brake may need it. [A64]
Source: [A64 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec17-R20 | anchor: A64
Brake smoke can warn of a runaway truck or bus, so move out of its path and do not enter ahead of it. [A64]
Source: [A64 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec17-R21 | anchor: A64
In construction zones, signs and markings may be missing; do not pull ahead of a truck or bus and stop abruptly. [A64]
Source: [A64 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec17-R22 | anchor: A64
Watch ahead for a bus’s frequent stops and change lanes before the stop if you need to avoid queuing behind it. [A64]
Source: [A64 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec17-R23 | anchor: A64
Pass a parked bus cautiously because it may reenter traffic and pedestrians or children may run in front of it. [A64]
Source: [A64 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec17-R24 | anchor: A64
An articulated bus has about 3 feet of tail swing, so leave enough room behind it for that movement. [A64]
Source: [A64 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec17-R25 | anchor: A64
Larger vehicles generally have greater blind spots, require more maneuver and stopping space, and take longer to accelerate or pass. [A64]
Source: [A64 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec17-R26 | anchor: A64
Smaller vehicles are harder for truck and bus drivers to see. [A64]
Source: [A64 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec17-R27 | anchor: A64
Yield to an emergency vehicle using flashing lights and a siren by moving toward the road edge without blocking an intersection. [A64]
Source: [A64 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec17-R28 | anchor: A64
During a police stop, move safely and promptly to the right outside the travel lane without obstructing other traffic. [A64]
Source: [A64 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec17-R29 | anchor: A64
Remain in the stopped vehicle unless the officer requests otherwise. [A64]
Source: [A64 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec17-R30 | anchor: A64
For the stop described in the handbook, turn off the engine, activate hazard lights, use interior lights at night and lower the window to communicate. [A64]
Source: [A64 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec17-R31 | anchor: A64
Stay calm with belts fastened, ask passengers to do the same, keep hands on the wheel and minimize unnecessary movement. [A64]
Source: [A64 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec17-R32 | anchor: A65
Provide license, insurance proof and registration when requested, first telling the officer where they are and reaching slowly with one hand kept on the wheel. [A65]
Source: [A65 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec17-R33 | anchor: A65
Answer the officer clearly and fully and never flee law enforcement. [A65]
Source: [A65 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec17-R34 | anchor: A65
A rear fluorescent or reflective orange-and-red triangle on slow equipment indicates travel below 25 miles per hour. [A65]
Source: [A65 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec17-R35 | anchor: A65
Approach slow vehicles cautiously and pass only when safe. [A65]
Source: [A65 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec17-R36 | anchor: A65
Watch rural roads for farm equipment crossing or traveling the highway, and do not assume its operator can hear an approaching car. [A65]
Source: [A65 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec17-R37 | anchor: A65
Animal-drawn vehicles and horseback riders have road-use rights and must follow road rules, so pass carefully. [A65]
Source: [A65 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec17-R38 | anchor: A65
Do not sound the horn or rev the engine near horses because frightening them can cause a crash. [A65]
Source: [A65 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec17-R39 | anchor: A65
Expect animal-drawn vehicles to turn left into fields or driveways and watch for posted warnings of these road users. [A65]
Source: [A65 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0065]
